text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] prod-us-west: GPU hotpath pool 'hp-usw-1' at 100% for 4m. 429s increasing on /v1/generate, queue depth trending up (q=120 -> 420). Paging oncall-gpu :rotating_light:
oncall-gpu: I’m on it. pulling metrics now. can someone post impact numbers?
support-lead: seeing customer error spikes — 3k 429s/min across the last 2m. top affected customers: finapp-x, chatco, learning-svc. likely user-facing for high-traffic routes.
morgan: any recent deploys or policy changes in the last 6h?
samir: there was a rate-policy canary this morning around 03:10 UTC that adjusted tier weights. I flagged one diff but it passed canary. suspect token refill/tier weight swap.
adele: running queries — `sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",code="429"}[1m])) by (tier)` shows majority from `standard` tier. token refill for standard looks very low (10 tokens/s) vs usual 80.
oncall-gpu: confirming logs from autoscaler: `scale_attempt: blocked by tier_quota check` at 03:12:09, followed by `hotpool_exhausted` entries. autoscaler tried to add nodes but hit policy limit for tier-bound pools.
morgan: ok two parallel mitigations: 1) widen token refill temporarily for standard tier 2) relax per-tier autoscale cap or route some traffic to fallback models. which is faster?
samir: fastest is token change via config-service. command: 
```
# increment token refill for standard
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/api/v1/ratepolicies/standard" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"token_refill": 240}'
```
this should cut 429s within 30-60s. fallback routing requires policy change + partial rollout -> ~5-10m.
oncall-gpu: doing token bump now. will also open autoscale cap ticket in parallel.
adele: running the POST now... 
`200 OK` returned. policy reload triggered: `policy-reload-id=rl-202403`.
support-lead: I told affected customers we have a mitigation in progress and ETA ~5m. they asked if data lost — responded requests are being throttled, no data loss.
morgan: also temporarily increasing hotpath autoscale cap for prod-us-west to allow +4 GPUs: 
```
rcli autoscale set-cap --pool hp-usw-1 --extra 4
```
deploy-bot: autoscale change initiated by morgan at 03:18 UTC, activity id asg-83421. expected spin-up ~2m per GPU.
oncall-gpu: metrics — 429s dropped from 3k/min -> 600/min in 90s after token bump. queue depth down to 80. autoscaler reports 2 new GPUs provisioning.
samir: good, keep an eye on latencies — we may get higher p95 if we let more small requests through. watch `p95_response_time`.
adele: p95 holding steady +80ms, ok. fallback model not required.
support-lead: customers reporting gradual recovery. finapp-x reported reduced errors in their dashboards.
morgan: root cause hypothesis: canary earlier inadvertently swapped tier weights between `premium` and `standard` which drove the standard tier’s token_refill down. Need to validate config changeset (CL 4728).
oncall-gpu: capturing timeline: 03:10 canary rollout; 03:12 first blocked scale; 03:15 token bump; 03:20 autoscale +2 GPUs active; 03:28 429s near baseline.
samir: immediate post-incident actions: revert the canary weight change, add config validation that flags token_refill < 50 for any customer-facing tier, and add a synthetic test that simulates burst to detect tier under-provision.
morgan: I'm doing a rollback of the canary now to be safe: 
```
configctl rollback --change 4728
```
rollback done: `ok`
deploy-bot: rollback completed, policy version v2024-03-10_4727 active.
oncall-gpu: confirming token_refill for standard now persisted at 240 after rollback? looks like the manual bump remained — we should decide final target.
support-lead: recommend keeping the bump for 2h while we validate, then tune back to normal 80 with canary test. notify customers again when fully resolved.
morgan: agreed. setting follow-up: postmortem owner samir, due EOD tomorrow. action items:
- samir: root cause analysis and config diff (CL 4728)
- devex: add unit test for policy validation (token_refill min)
- infra: add autoscaler guard to allow emergency bursts even when tier caps low
- support: customer follow-up note with timeline

samir: noted, will own.
oncall-gpu: marking incident as mitigated in incident tracker. `incident-bot` please create incident record and tag SEV-3 transient production throttling.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-347. severity: SEV-3. timeline attached.
support-lead: closing customer updates loop now. will reopen slack thread if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
morgan: great work team. quick retrospective: add pre-deploy guard for policy diffs that change refill by >50% and an automated smoke that hits /v1/generate 5k qps for 30s in canary to detect this earlier.
samir: adding notes to the RCA. we'll schedule follow-up in eng-weekly.
